messages.content:
You finish a dry-stone wall. The wall is built course by course with Wang's method; you act only at the end, when every remaining stone is on offer. At each placement you choose which candidate to place: a stone in one of four rotations, at the position Wang's image convolution found for it. Every listed candidate is feasible (LLC > 0). Your goal is the finished wall, judged on four metrics: F_SF, stone filling (the share of the wall area that is stone, higher is better); F_AH, the horizontal joint path index (lower is better: no long continuous horizontal joints); F_AV, the vertical joint path index (higher is better: vertical joints are staggered); F_LR, the smaller of the left and right kinematic limit loads of the wall divided by the friction coefficient (higher is better). A stone that cannot be placed is lost to the wall.
Data. Stones are labelled S1, S2, ... in the order they were first sampled. Coordinates are pixels in the evaluation frame (mirrored when building from the right, so 'left' is the side the course is built from); rows count upward from the ground. Each candidate: id, stone, rotation, its pose x and y, the width and height of its bounding box, and Wang's five filter scores (higher is better for each): NHR course height (0 = level with its left neighbour), GDS global density, IWR interlocking (its vertical joint far from the joints below), LLC the kinematic limit load of the wall with the stone added and stabilized, divided by the friction coefficient, LFR local void (0 = flush on the left and on the bottom). wall summarizes the current wall; unplaceable lists stones on offer with no feasible candidate now. Nothing about the final wall is known.
Compare the main candidates on all five scores and on what they leave for the remaining stones; in the rationale state each one's main advantages and costs. Finish with commit_pick.

arguments.rationale:
Choose S16 at 0°: GDS is 1.0 as for every candidate; its IWR 1.160 is the best, LLC 0.517 is tied for best, and LFR -0.037 is relatively flush. NHR -0.366 is a moderate course-height mismatch, worse than the best levelling choices. Its 103-pixel width uses substantial space, but its interlocking and support make it a strong balance for filling, stagger and stability.

S3 at 180° (9) levels better (NHR -0.111), is slightly more flush (LFR -0.030), and has the same GDS and LLC, but much weaker IWR 0.345 and a smaller 85×27 footprint. S15 at 180° (7) has a larger 129×53 footprint and the same GDS/LLC, but worse NHR -0.509, IWR 0.280 and LFR -0.060. S4 at 0° (3) also has the same GDS/LLC and strong IWR 0.954, but poor NHR -0.963 and LFR -0.128. S2 at 90° (5) is more level and flush (NHR -0.241, LFR -0.023), with the same GDS/LLC, but almost no interlocking (IWR 0.044). S3 at 270° (12) has NHR -0.165, LFR -0.024 and the same GDS/LLC, but IWR 0.403 and a tall narrow footprint. S13 at 180° (11) is the flushest (LFR -0.014) and has the same GDS/LLC, but NHR -0.667 and IWR 0.098 are weak; its thin shape may be useful in a later gap.

Choosing S16 leaves the other stones available, including the larger S15 and S4 and the thin S13, but changes the skyline and could make their present poses infeasible. S9 has no feasible pose now, though its later feasibility is unknown. No candidate scores guarantee final filling, joint paths or limit load.

arguments.rationale:
Pick S15 at 180°: its large, low profile uses a potentially difficult stone while giving the best NHR (-0.170), full GDS (1.0), reasonable IWR (0.537), and the common best LLC (0.517). Its LFR (-0.119) is a cost, and its long footprint near the right edge may restrict later placements or encourage a horizontal joint. It leaves S2, S3, S4, S9 and S13; their future feasibility is unknown.

The strongest alternative is S4 at 0°: NHR -0.204, GDS 1.0, best IWR 0.838, LLC 0.517 and better LFR -0.061. It favors stagger and tighter packing, but leaves the large S15, whose only other current option is tall and poorly matched. S4 at 180° is nearly identical on NHR, GDS, IWR and LFR (-0.204, 1.0, 0.836, -0.063), but has lower LLC (0.345). S4 at 270° has weaker scores (-0.505, 0.914, 0.217, 0.517, -0.132) and a taller profile.

S2 at 0° packs tightly (-0.246, 1.0, 0.159, 0.517, -0.047), but has poor interlocking and leaves both large stones. Its 180° option improves IWR to 0.568 but worsens NHR and LFR to -0.947 and -0.167, with GDS 1.0 and LLC 0.517. S3 has good IWR and LFR (-0.519, 1.0, 0.574, 0.517, -0.034), but is thin and leaves the large stones. S13 is the flushest (-0.667, 1.0, 0.098, 0.517, -0.014), yet its very thin shape and weak interlocking offer limited progress. S9 at 180° has scores -0.242, 1.0, 0.256, 0.345, -0.109: reasonably level but weaker interlocking and load. S9 at 90° scores -0.604, 0.882, 0.140, 0.517, -0.190; S15 at 90° scores -0.628, 0.0, 0.286, 0.517, -0.159. Both tall alternatives have substantial density or void costs. These are immediate tradeoffs, not guarantees about final wall metrics or subsequent feasibility.
